problem:
Implement exactly these rules; they were proven against the whole test suite. Add one new pass, refineHunks, to packages/element/src/textDiff.ts. Change nothing else in diffText except the three return points below. Keep the existing helpers, meter charges and exports as they are.

New module constant after the other constants: const WORD_CHARACTER = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;

New helpers placed just above `export const diffText`:

1. isInsideWord(text: string, at: number): true when at > 0 and at < text.length and WORD_CHARACTER matches both text[at - 1] and text[at].

2. splitsSurrogatePair(text: string, at: number): true when at > 0 and at < text.length and text.charCodeAt(at - 1) is a high surrogate and text.charCodeAt(at) is a low surrogate (use isHighSurrogate and isLowSurrogate).

3. alignLines(oldText, newText, hunk): TextHunk[] | null. Split oldText.slice(hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd) and newText.slice(hunk.newStart, hunk.newEnd) on "\n". Return null if there are fewer than 2 old lines or the two line counts differ. Otherwise walk the lines with oldAt = hunk.oldStart and newAt = hunk.newStart. For line i, oldEnd = oldAt + old line length and newEnd = newAt + new line length; push trimHunk(oldText, newText, { oldStart: oldAt, oldEnd, newStart: newAt, newEnd }, true, true); then oldAt = oldEnd + 1 and newAt = newEnd + 1. Return the list. Each newline between lines is kept unchanged.

4. alignToken(oldText, newText, hunk): TextHunk[] | null. length = hunk.oldEnd - hunk.oldStart. Return null if length < 1, or length >= MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, or hunk.newEnd - hunk.newStart <= length, or isInsideWord(oldText, hunk.oldStart), or isInsideWord(oldText, hunk.oldEnd). token = oldText.slice(hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd). Return null if token.trim() === "". For at from hunk.newStart while at + length <= hunk.newEnd, ascending: if newText.startsWith(token, at) and not isInsideWord(newText, at) and not isInsideWord(newText, at + length) and not splitsSurrogatePair(newText, at) and not splitsSurrogatePair(newText, at + length), return the two hunks { oldStart: hunk.oldStart, oldEnd: hunk.oldStart, newStart: hunk.newStart, newEnd: at } and { oldStart: hunk.oldEnd, oldEnd: hunk.oldEnd, newStart: at + length, newEnd: hunk.newEnd }. Return null when the loop ends.

5. getSlide(changed, other, start, end, at, lower, upper): number. changed is the text holding the hunk's span [start, end); other is the opposite text; at is the hunk's position in other; lower and upper bound the span. Return 0 if not isInsideWord(other, at). Let canLeft = true and canRight = true. For step from 1 to end - start inclusive:
- canLeft = canLeft && start - step >= lower && changed[start - step] === changed[end - step]. If canLeft and not isInsideWord(other, at - step) and not splitsSurrogatePair(changed, start - step) and not splitsSurrogatePair(changed, end - step), return -step.
- canRight = canRight && end + step <= upper && changed[start + step - 1] === changed[end + step - 1]. If canRight and not isInsideWord(other, at + step) and not splitsSurrogatePair(changed, start + step) and not splitsSurrogatePair(changed, end + step), return step.
- If neither canLeft nor canRight, stop the loop.
Return 0 after the loop.

6. refineHunks(oldText, newText, hunks: readonly TextHunk[], meter: DiffMeter): TextHunk[].
First pass, aligned: TextHunk[] = []. For each hunk: oldLength and newLength are its side lengths. If meter.left <= 0 or oldLength === 0 or newLength === 0, push the hunk as it is and continue. Otherwise meter.left -= oldLength + newLength, then push alignLines(...) if it is not null, else alignToken(...) if it is not null, else the hunk.
Then parts = aligned without hunks that are empty on both sides (keep a hunk when oldStart < oldEnd or newStart < newEnd).
Second pass, for i over parts: hunk = parts[i]; isInsertion = oldStart === oldEnd; isDeletion = newStart === newEnd. If meter.left <= 0 or neither is true, continue. previous = parts[i - 1], next = parts[i + 1]. meter.left -= (oldEnd - oldStart) + (newEnd - newStart). slide = for an insertion getSlide(newText, oldText, hunk.newStart, hunk.newEnd, hunk.oldStart, previous ? previous.newEnd : 0, next ? next.newStart : newText.length); for a deletion getSlide(oldText, newText, hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd, hunk.newStart, previous ? previous.oldEnd : 0, next ? next.oldStart : oldText.length). parts[i] = the hunk with slide added to all four fields. Note parts[i - 1] is read after it may have slid. Return parts.

The three changes in diffText, and no others:
(a) The early-return condition with four tests becomes three separate checks in this order. If trimmed.oldEnd - trimmed.oldStart + (trimmed.newEnd - trimmed.newStart) < MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, return [trimmed]. If oldText.length < MIN_MATCH_LENGTH or newText.length < MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, return refineHunks(oldText, newText, [trimmed], meter). If indexWork > meter.left, return [trimmed]. So a typed character keeps its fast path and spends nothing, and an empty meter still returns the trimmed hunk.
(b) `if (blocks.length === 0) { return [trimmed]; }` now returns refineHunks(oldText, newText, [trimmed], meter).
(c) The final return passes the existing filtered gaps through refineHunks(oldText, newText, <the filtered gaps>, meter).

Add four tests through the real editor, following this file's existing Tab and Shift+Tab tests exactly, and change no existing test. Each sets a style on one character by setSelectionRange and the action, then selects all lines and presses Tab or Shift+Tab as those tests do, then asserts the true offset and that the styled text is the same character.
1. Tab on all lines of a note of 500 one-character lines, letters from a to z repeating, joined by "\n" (999 characters): colour the character of line 250. After Tab the run is on that line's character, at its offset plus (250 + 1) * 4.
2. Shift+Tab on the same note with every line first indented by 4 spaces: colour line 250's letter. After Shift+Tab the run is on that letter, at its offset less (250 + 1) * 4.
3. Tab on all lines of a 200-line note where line i is "x" when i % 3 === 0, else `line number ${i} of the note`: colour the "x" of line 99. After Tab the run is on that "x" at its offset plus (99 + 1) * 4.
4. Tab on a note of the five lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: colour "3". After Tab the run is on "3" at offset 4 + 3 * 4.
Do not loosen an assertion to pass.
